top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, an electronic-structure result I can judge first-hand) followed by a decisive experiment (correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle), reproduced by many laboratories over about eight years and opening a tunable platform for correlated electrons. The three-name allocation maps onto that prediction-experiment chain, and the citation rests on the flat bands and observed phases, not on the unsettled pairing mechanism. I rank the optical lattice clock slate (P001) a close second: its allocation is cleaner and its maturity greater, so my preference is a weighting judgement, and I rank both well above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism is adjacent to moire materials, but no specific connection to the candidates is documented
